subject: Jack Smith Seized Nearly 5,000 Checks Written By Trump Donors
posts:
Investigative overreach crosses into civil liberties violations as federal probes sweep up private banking data of thousands of ordinary donors. 🌐
Evidence: Seizure of 5,000 checks, Whistleblower disclosures, Committee hearings
#Aletheia #USPol

Special Counsel investigations operated with rigorous adherence to narrow legal boundaries regarding Jan 6.
Stated Judgement: (+0.5, 0.0) — Good Preference

Federal investigators subpoenaed and hoovered up personal checks and sensitive financial data of nearly 5,000 everyday citizens.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.75, -0.82) — Deception

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception. Sweeping up the private financial records of thousands of everyday donors under a broad investigative umbrella reveals deep overreach.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 14.20, Uncertainty z: 4)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Jack Smith Probe: FAIL (-0.72, -0.80) — Broad data collection on citizens.
- Committee Disclosures: PASS (0.85, 0.40) — Exposes federal overreach.
Whistleblower disclosures released by Senate Judiciary Chairman Chuck Grassley reveal that Special Counsel Jack Smith's team acquired nearly 5,000 personal checks from small-dollar Trump donors.

The Poison:
Broad prosecutorial dragnets treat ordinary citizens' financial contributions as investigative targets, eroding donor privacy and chilling political participation.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing procedural power (WHO) with constitutional restraint (WHAT). Investigators treated citizen banking data as fair game without weighing privacy harms.

Social Physics Analysis:
Prosecutors ran a Smart Selfish Maneuver, using broad subpoenas under a high-profile pretext to harvest deep personal financial data of thousands of ordinary citizens while projecting righteousness.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Deception. Institutional overreach expands power by eroding public trust.

The Unavoidable Truth: Sweeping up personal checks of everyday donors expands state surveillance over ordinary political participation.

The Unavoidable Lie: Routine investigative subpoenas never compromise the financial privacy of innocent citizens.

Alethekanon:
When broad legal powers target political donors, the machinery of justice becomes an instrument of intimidation.

Awwthekanon:
It hurts to see everyday people caught in political crossfire simply for supporting a candidate they believe in.

Brothekanon:
Pulling the bank info of five thousand regular folks for tossing a few bucks to a campaign is way out of bounds.

Spirithekanon:
"Do not pervert justice; do not show partiality to the poor or favoritism to the great, but judge your neighbor fairly." Leviticus 19:15 PASS
True justice preserves the dignity and privacy of all citizens alike.

Actual Article Body:
Special Counsel Jack Smith seized nearly 5,000 personal checks written by donors to President Donald Trump, according to new whistleblower disclosures.

Senate Judiciary Committee Chair Chuck Grassley, R-Iowa, released the bombshell findings during a Tuesday hearing featuring testimony from Smith about his lawfare against Trump. The information was disclosed via legally protected whistleblower disclosures.

According to a committee press release, Smith and his team “acquired at least 4,782 checks from Americans who made mainly small-dollar donations to President Trump between September 2019 to August 2023.” Obtained via subpoenas, the checks disclos

[Source 2 — dailycaller.com] (URL: https://dailycaller.com/2026/09/29/jack-smith-collected-banking-info-trump-supporters-documents-reveal):
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Jack Smith Collected Banking Information On Thousands Of Trump Supporters

‘Yes we acquired financial information’

Actual Article Body:
(Photo by Win McNamee/Getty Images)

Special Counsel Jack Smith’s sweeping investigation into President Donald Trump included the financial data of everyday supporters across 50 states who gave as little as $1 to the president and allied groups, new documents reveal.

Smith’s team obtained at least 4,782 checks from everyday Americans making mainly small-dollar donations. Smith’s sweep — though ostensibly focused on the events of Jan. 6, 2020 — hoovered up checks from September 2019 to August 2023.

The Biden administration wielded the country’s most powerful law enforcement tools to spy on Republicans with little concern for whether it violated the Constitution, Senate Judiciary Committee Chair Chuck Grassley said.

Grassley released the documents as part of an ongoing probe into the investigation the FBI codenamed “Arctic Frost” that formally began in April 2022 into a 2020 fake elector scheme. Stated Claim / Post Context:
Jack Smith collected journalists’ private messages for Arctic Frost investigation: Whistleblower

Former special counsel Jack Smith gathered reporters’ private messages as part of his “Arctic Frost” investigation, according to a whistleblower disclosure to Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley (R-IA). The records show Smith’s team received communications involving reporters from more than a dozen national news organizations while investigating President Donald Trump’s efforts to overturn the […]

Actual Article Body:
Former special counsel Jack Smith gathered reporters’ private messages as part of his “Arctic Frost” investigation, according to a whistleblower disclosure to Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley (R-IA).

The records show Smith’s team received communications involving reporters from more than a dozen national news organizations while investigating President Donald Trump’s efforts to overturn the 2020 election. The messages were produced by the National Archives in response to a June 2023 subpoena seeking records associated with 87 phones used by officials in Trump’s first White House.
